items.evidence: vitest earlier-showdowns acceptance 'a replaced bot never sees...' passes on branch and fails on base. The test compares each view against a per-tenure model built from showdownOf and replaced, and asserts forgotten > 0. Holdout check: runPlaytest with a recording policy across 6 scenarios. Five cash scenarios (Tough 6 seats seed 42 2000h: 217 replacements, 3020 forgotten shown hands; Soft 9 seats 2000h: 482 replacements; Mixed 6 and 9 seats check-down 2500/2200h; no line-up 1600h) plus a 600h sng. Every view equalled an independently built windowed model (append, cap 1000, then forget the next hand's replaced seats). An independent tenure check, which traces each shown hand back to a hand at or after its seat's arrival, found 0 violations. Seat 1 was never replaced.

vitest 'every earlier showdown a policy receives is frozen' passes on branch and fails on base. Holdout: every non-empty list in every scenario was deep-frozen (0 failures over about 350k views). 7 kinds of tampering (push, pop, assign entry.shown, delete entry.shown, push to shown, assign seat, assign holeCards[0]) gave TypeErrors 488040/488040, 419573/419573 and 81613/81613. Later views still equalled the model.

unit test passes and asserts length, copy (not the same object), deep freeze, and that the input list and entry are unchanged and not frozen. Holdout: limit 1 keeps only the newest; the caller's entry stays unfrozen and is copied; after 1200 appends at limit 1000 the list has exactly 1000 entries, keeps the newest, and is deep-frozen. In runs the list length reached exactly 1000 and never more.

unit test passes: the worked example, the untouched entry is the same object, [] and [7] return the same list, multiple seats. Holdout: forgetting every seat returns an empty frozen list; a non-matching seat returns the same list; seats [1,3,3] with a duplicate over 1000 entries leave 600, deep-frozen, with none of those seats left.
